headline: Broad growth across all divisions lifts revenue and profit
summary_short: Nasdaq reported Q2 2026 net revenue of $1.50B (+14.9% y/y) and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.89 (+14.1% y/y), with net income of $507M and Index ETP AUM surpassing $1 trillion for the first time.
summary_long: Net revenue rose 14.9% y/y (+6.6% q/q) to $1.50B on 17% Solutions growth (Capital Access Platforms + Financial Technology) and a 38% Index revenue jump aided by a one-time contract-modification benefit. GAAP operating income grew 25.4% y/y to $712M; net income was $507M (+12.2% y/y) and GAAP diluted EPS $0.89 (+14.1% y/y; non-GAAP EPS $1.07, +25%). The company returned $174M via dividends and $356M via buybacks, with $2.5B left under its authorization, and net repaid $162M of debt. Cash fell 29% y/y to $520M on debt paydown and capital returns. Nasdaq updated FY2026 non-GAAP opex guidance to $2.530-2.570B and maintained its 22.5-24.5% tax-rate guidance.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited 'an outstanding second quarter' with double-digit growth across all three divisions, $1 trillion+ in Index ETP AUM, and the SpaceX listing as the largest IPO in exchange history.

Solutions revenue grew 17% on strength across Capital Access Platforms and Financial Technology; Index revenue grew 38%, aided by a one-time contract-modification benefit disclosed in the adjusted-variance footnote.
Revenue growth of 15% outpaced GAAP operating expense growth of 7%, partially offset by lower merger and strategic-initiatives expense.
Not explained separately from the pretax income drivers above; the effective tax rate rose to 22.4% from 17.5% a year ago.
EPS grew faster than net income because weighted diluted shares fell 1.9% y/y, reflecting continued buybacks ($356M repurchased this quarter).
Cash fell 29% y/y after the company returned $174M via dividends and $356M via buybacks and net repaid $162M of debt in the quarter.
